subject: SLA amendment request — maintenance carveouts & monthly credit cap
messages:
From: Samir Khatri <samir.k@orioncloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@orioncloud.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA carveout for scheduled maintenance windows + monthly credit cap

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the productive demo earlier this week. As we map Redwood into our infra plan, procurement asked me to formalize a couple of asks tied to availability/credits so we can present a clean one-page to our legal team. High level:

- We run a global maintenance cadence that sometimes requires multi-region takeovers; for the first 6 months we need an explicit carveout for a monthly 4-hour maintenance window per region (roughly 02:00–06:00 PT first Sunday) where standard uptime calculations do not trigger credits.
- For predictable budgeting we also need a firm cap on monthly service credits (not a percentage of annual fees) — ideally a cap equal to 15% of a single monthly committed invoice while we ramp usage.

Attached is our annotated redline of Redwood's standard SLA template (Orion_SLA_Template_redlines.pdf). Can you confirm if Redwood can either accept these two items or propose reasonable alternatives?

CCing procurement to keep the thread in one place (procurement@orioncloud.com).

Appreciate a quick confirmation of next steps — our board wants to sign by mid-September if we can get terms agreed.

Best,
Samir Khatri
Head of Platform Ops, OrionCloud
samir.k@orioncloud.com
[Attachment: Orion_SLA_Template_redlines.pdf (PDF)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Samir Khatri <samir.k@orioncloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for scheduled maintenance windows + monthly credit cap

Samir —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redlines (we reviewed the PDF). We can work with you on a bounded carveout and a credit cap, but there are a few trade-offs we need to align on before we can accept the exact language:

1) Carveout window: we can agree to a scheduled maintenance carveout (first Sunday, 02:00–06:00 PT per region) for the first 6 months, provided outages outside of scheduled windows continue to count toward uptime. We will include a requirement that Redirect notices for maintenance are published 72 hours in advance.

2) Monthly credit cap: we cannot accept a fixed percentage of the monthly invoice that exceeds our financial guardrails. As a compromise, we propose a cap equal to 10% of the monthly committed invoice during the 6-month ramp; after that we can revisit based on actual usage and mean-time-to-recover metrics.

3) Latency SLOs: for batch/ingest jobs with predictable tails we can trade a slightly relaxed latency SLO in off-peak windows in exchange for the credit cap (details below).

Ben and Marissa are looped in — Ben, can you confirm commercial feasibility with a 12-month minimum commitment in exchange for the above concessions? Marissa, could you propose the technical carveouts and mitigation (routing to fallback model variants / regional failover) and attach any operational guidelines we should include?

Next steps: once we have agreement on the cap and the scheduled window language, legal can ship a short amendment (SLA_Amendment_ORC-4931.docx) for signature.

Thanks,

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA carveout for scheduled maintenance windows + monthly credit cap

Hi all —

Operational notes from the SRE/Product side:

- Scheduled maintenance carveout: acceptable. We'll formalize an "advance notification" clause (72 hours) and a change window soft limit (max 4 hours per region per month; any additional planned activity requires coordination).
- Regional failover: we will enable smart routing to healthy regions during the carveout windows where feasible; however, customers must accept transient latency increases for cross-region failovers.
- Latency SLO adjustment: propose an off-peak tail latency SLO of p95 < 800ms and p99 < 2.1s for bulk batch windows during the carveout period. Production, latency SLOs remain unchanged for peak interactive routes.
- Monitoring & Reporting: we'll attach a monthly uptime/incident summary to the customer console and provide raw incident logs on audit request (subject to standard redaction).

Attaching an internal operations note (maintenance_policies.pdf) that outlines the rollback/mitigation playbook and the fallback model variant behavior.

If this reads OK to procurement, legal can accept the wording below and I will sign off on the operational guarantees.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Reliability | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Proposed SLA amendment language & next steps (SLA amendment attached)

Samir / Orion procurement team —

Thanks for the patience while we lined up commercial and operational approvals. Summary of the agreed position we will put into the amendment:

- Scheduled maintenance carveout: first Sunday monthly, 02:00–06:00 PT per region for 6 months. Redwood will post a 72-hour maintenance notice in the customer console. Outages outside the carveout still count against uptime.
- Monthly service credit cap: capped at 10% of the monthly committed invoice during the 6-month ramp period (not per-incident).
- Latency: interactive routes unchanged. Off-peak/bulk windows: p95 < 800ms, p99 < 2.1s while running fallback/regional failover.
- Commitment: Redwood will require a 12-month minimum committed term to enable these concessions (deal ORC-4931).

Attached: SLA_Amendment_ORC-4931.docx (short legal amendment reflecting the above). Procurement, if acceptable please confirm the billing contact and we will issue a DocuSign for signature. Planned timeline: send DocuSign by 2026-09-05, signed by 2026-09-12 to make the board window.

If there's anything you want tightened in the amendment text (e.g., defining the formula for monthly invoice), flag it now — otherwise we'll proceed on the timeline above.

Best,
